blocks.passage:
Trade credit is when a seller lets the buyer pay later — often 30, 60 or 90 days after delivery. It is one of the oldest forms of business finance.

Why offer it? Because it helps win customers and sell more. A buyer with a little more time to pay usually comes back for another order.

There is a cost, of course. The seller must wait for the money and carry a small risk. That is why trade credit is, in the end, a kind of loan.

audio.text:
You're new to sales, and you asked why we offer sixty days of trade credit to our best clients when we could ask for the money right away. Good question — let me explain.

Imagine two suppliers selling the same coffee at the same price. One says 'pay me today, on delivery'. The other says 'take the coffee now, pay me in sixty days'. Which one gets the order? Almost always the second. The buyer keeps their cash longer, so they prefer that supplier.

So trade credit is a tool to win business. It's like saying 'I trust you — enjoy the goods now, pay me later'. Clients like that, and they come back.

But it's not free for us. For those sixty days, we've delivered the coffee but we don't have the money. We're basically lending it to them. So we only offer it to clients we trust, and we set a limit on how much.

The rule is simple: offer credit to good clients to win more orders, but never more than you can afford to wait for.
